name: Peristaltic catheter
full_name: Peristaltically propelled active catheter: hydraulic two-balloon self-propelling catheter for the radial artery, driven by motorised syringes
group: Nippon Institute of Technology, Department of Innovative Systems Engineering (Yuichi Nakazato, K. Takita, M. Higuchi; K. Kawanaka) (nakazato2017_peristaltic p. 79)
versions: 2010: in-pipe micro mobile robot using peristalsis, hydraulic (nakazato2010_inpipe, J. Mech. Sci. Technol. 24:51-54; MAMM 2010), the mechanism the lab later tested 'using pseudoblood vessels with an inner diameter of <=6 mm ... assuming that the catheter is inserted in a femoral artery' (nakazato2017 Abstract; 2010 papers title only) -> 2016/2017: radial-artery catheter, section A 5 mm + section B 5/6/7 mm, phi 2.0 x 23.0 mm (nakazato2017_peristaltic Sec. 3.1, Figs. 2-3; MAMM-2016 proceedings, Springer 2017)
target_anatomy: radial-artery access for coronary treatment (radial ID 2.0-3.5 mm, Abstract); tested in silicone tubes of ID 2.5 and 3.0 mm and in the right internal and external carotid arteries of an endovascular surgery simulator (EVE, FAIN-Biomedical) (Sec. 4.2, 5.2)
devices_driven: its own active catheter, self-propelled: 'a self-propelled active catheter was realized without a guide wire' (Sec. 2); no off-the-shelf device
n_dof_detail: 1: forward locomotion by a travelling wave of two alternately inflated sections A and B; no steering, no rotation (Sec. 2, Fig. 1)
translation_detail: other: peristaltic self-propulsion inside the vessel: saline pressure-fed and aspirated alternately in balloon sections A and B, which grip the wall by friction and extend (Sec. 2, Fig. 1)
device_range: catheter phi 2.0 mm x 23.0 mm, feeding pipe phi 0.4 mm (Fig. 3); balloon sections of silicone rubber OD 0.8 mm, wall 0.12 mm, joined by silicone tubes OD 0.4 / ID 0.3 mm (Sec. 3.1)
footprint_mm: actuator: two syringe-and-linear-slider units in parallel, each 323.5 x 111.0 mm (Figs. 4-5 captions); connected to the catheter by a 1 m silicone tube (ID 0.5, OD 1.0 mm) (Sec. 3.2)
haptics_leader: none (feed sequence of the two syringes; operator interface N.R.)
validation_detail: phantom: forward driving over 30 mm in silicone tubes (ID 2.5 and 3.0 mm, Young's modulus 1.7 MPa, water-glycerin pseudo-blood 5.0 mPa s) at feeding rates 140-570 ul/s (Sec. 4.2-4.4, Table 1, Fig. 7); EVE simulator: moved forward in the right internal and external carotid arteries at radii of curvature up to 1.2 cm, moved backward at 0.8 cm (Sec. 5.3, Fig. 9). Number of runs N.R.
key_numbers: max speed 4.79 mm/s at 570 ul/s and 370 ul feed (Sec. 4.4); design target 5 mm/s (Sec. 3.1); feed volume 230-400 ul (Sec. 4.3); catheter phi 2.0 x 23.0 mm (Fig. 3)

notes: N3 2026-11-08, from review_comparison Sec. 1.3 (Alekseeva Table 14 row 6, 'Peristaltically Propelled Active Catheter', ex vivo phantom TRL3). In scope as an actuated device: the catheter moves itself inside vessel models by fluid pressure, and the fluid is moved by syringes on electric sliders 'consisting of a stepping motor and ball screws' (XA-42-D, SUS Corp., Sec. 3.2). Alekseeva's 2010 reference is an in-pipe robot, not a catheter. Main picture is the drive; the catheter itself (Fig. 3) is in the gallery.
